mlxtrx

mlxtrx launches Monolix, PKanalix and Simulx runs and keeps a record of each one: what ran, with which settings and files, when, and by whom. Every file is fingerprinted by its SHA-256 hash, so at any time you can ask whether the results on disk still match the files that produced them.

  • Launch many models in one call, on the grid (mono24, pk24, sim24) or locally (monolix.sh, pkanalix.sh, simulx.sh).
  • Detect whether each run succeeded and extract its fit statistics.
  • Get one condition per model, file or folder: never run, failed, unfinished, inputs changed, output edited, or clean.
  • Check the export settings MonolixSuite needs before launching.
  • Collect every run in one data frame to sort, filter or export.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("nash-delcamp-slp/mlxtrx")

Set the run store

Runs are recorded in a store: a folder of plain JSON files, one folder per run. Point mlxtrx at it once per session, usually from the project’s .Rprofile:

options(mlxtrx.store = "/path/to/<project>/monolix/.mlxtrx")

Every function also takes store = directly. Without either, mlxtrx stops and tells you how to set it. The store is created when the first run is recorded.

Launch runs 

library(mlxtrx)

run_ids <- mono(c("base/run1.mlxtran", "base/run2.mlxtran"), thread = 4)
pk("nca/<study>_nca.pkx")
sim("sim/<project>_sim.smlx")

mono() and pk() first check the charts-data export settings in the tool’s config.ini (check_config_ini()). All three record each run as it is submitted, wait for the grid jobs to leave the queue, then record the outputs and statistics. The default commands are mono24, pk24 and sim24; set options(mlxtrx.monolix_cmd = ), mlxtrx.pkanalix_cmd or mlxtrx.simulx_cmd, or pass cmd =, to use another command such as a local monolix.sh.

Projects built or edited with lixoftConnectors: save them with saveProject(), then run them with mono() or pk().

Check status 

run_status("base")
print_report_summary("base")
#> === RUN STATUS REPORT ===
#> Path: /path/to/<project>/monolix/base
#> ...
#> Models: 3
#>   inputs_changed  1
#>   clean           2
#>
#> Needs attention:
#>   run2.mlxtran  inputs_changed
#>     data/<study>_pk.csv modified

run_status() returns one row per model with a single condition, most serious first: never_run, untracked_results (results in the model’s output folder that no recorded run produced, e.g. from the GUI or lixoftConnectors), failed, unfinished, inputs_changed, output_edited, output_suspect, clean_late, clean. A file that no run recorded is untracked. Pass a folder, a project file, or any input or output file. print_report_summary() prints the same result as a report.

The check_*() functions answer narrower questions about project, input and output files.

Archive key runs 

archive_run("base/run3.mlxtran")
run_status("base")$archived

archive_run() keeps an exact copy of a model’s latest run: the project file, its inputs, its outputs and the run’s config.ini copy. Each file is stored once under its SHA-256 in <store>/objects (set options(mlxtrx.archive = ) for another folder), so a data set shared by several runs is stored once. The run must be clean or clean_late. The project folder is not touched and stays usable.

verify_archive() re-hashes every archived file and reports each one as ok, missing or mismatch.

run_id <- run_status("base/run3.mlxtran")$run_id
restore_run(run_id, "restored/run3")
# add the data and config files to that restore
restore_run(run_id, "restored/run3", project = FALSE, outputs = FALSE,
            data = TRUE, config = TRUE)
retrieve_file(run_id, "base/data/pk.csv", "old")

restore_run() writes an archived run’s files under to in the same folder layout, so the restored project finds the restored copies of files under the store’s folder. By default it restores the project and outputs and leaves out the model and data (model = FALSE, data = FALSE), since those are often shared files maintained elsewhere; for each one left out it says whether the file now at its original path matches the archived copy. config = TRUE adds the config file and the run’s config.ini. Files with an absolute path outside the store’s folder go under to/_absolute/; the project file is not rewritten, so it still points at the original location, and a warning names each such file and its restored copy. Nothing is written if any target file already exists or any archived copy fails its hash check. Called interactively without any of these arguments, it shows a menu of the groups with their file counts and sizes, the defaults marked (default). retrieve_file() writes one archived file. If the archive folder has moved, pass its new location as archive = to verify_archive(), restore_run() or retrieve_file().

Results table

runs_data() returns every recorded run as one data frame, newest first: project, data and model files, settings, command, software version, user, times and state. Sort, filter or export it like any data frame.

runs <- runs_data(include_summary = TRUE, latest_only = TRUE)
write.csv(runs, "runs.csv", row.names = FALSE)
get_run_files(runs$run_id[1])

Statistics include, for Monolix, the values from summary.txt and observation counts; for PKanalix, the tasks run, the number of individuals, the compartmental analysis criteria and the bioequivalence ratios; for Simulx, the tasks run. get_run_files() lists every input and output file of a run with its SHA-256 hash. source_note() turns the plot or table data files behind a figure or table into a one-line footnote naming their runs, for TFL footnotes.

When a session dies

If the R session that launched runs ends before they finish, their completion is not recorded. Record it later with:

finalize_runs()

These runs are marked as recorded late, and any output written well after the rest of the run’s outputs is flagged as suspect.
